title: Your Patronus is built from one memory
dek: Not the happiest day of your life. The one that comes back on its own, at the exact moment you need it. Twelve questions, one memory, one animal.

results.name: THE KITCHEN AT ONE IN THE MORNING
results.blurb: One lamp, two chairs, somebody eating cereal standing up because sitting down would mean admitting it's late. Nobody is fixing anything. Nobody has to. This is the memory that comes back when the room is too quiet: not a triumph, just proof that you have been safe and known and awake with someone.
strengths: Finds safety in small, ordinary things
Makes people feel at home immediately
Calm at hours when nobody else is
results.watchOut: You keep waiting for that hour to come back. Make a new one this week.

results.name: THE LAST DAY OF SCHOOL
results.blurb: The bell, the noise, the corridor suddenly too small for everyone in it. Somebody signed your shirt. Somebody you never spoke to hugged you. You remember the heat and the terror of the next thing and how, for about forty minutes, none of it mattered. That is the feeling: the door opening all at once.
strengths: Turns a crowd into a team
results.watchOut: You keep chasing the feeling of a last day. Ordinary Tuesdays count too.

results.name: THE DOG AT THE DOOR
results.blurb: You come round the corner and something is already there, absolutely certain you were coming back. No conditions, no questions about where you've been. Of all the things you have been given in your life, this is the one your brain reaches for first, because it is the simplest possible proof that you are loved.
strengths: Makes coming home a real thing
results.watchOut: You'd wait at the door for people who don't come back. Set a limit.

results.name: THE CAR RIDE IN THE RAIN
results.blurb: Bad visibility, the wrong exit, a song you both knew every word to and sang anyway. Nothing was resolved in that car. Everything was survivable in that car. You remember the windscreen wipers more than you remember the conversation, and that is exactly why it works.
strengths: Finds the funny side of a disaster
results.watchOut: You'll stay in the car to avoid the conversation. Park it eventually.

results.name: THE POOL IN AUGUST
results.blurb: Chlorine, hot concrete, someone's radio, the specific ceiling of a summer afternoon when nothing has to happen until dinner. You were not happy because everything was good. You were happy because nothing was being asked of you, and that turned out to be the rarest thing of all.
strengths: Brings the holiday energy with you
Refuses to rush a nice afternoon
results.watchOut: You wait all year for August. Build small Augusts into the other months.

results.name: THE FIRST SNOW, NO PLANS
results.blurb: You woke up, looked out, and the whole day quietly cancelled itself. Nobody had to be anywhere. The street went silent, the kettle went on, and you stood at the window not thinking about anything at all. Peace, it turns out, is a weather condition you have been trying to recreate ever since.
strengths: Deeply comfortable in your own company
results.watchOut: Solitude is a gift until it becomes a habit. Open the door sometimes.

results.name: THE WRONG TURN THAT BECAME THE TRIP
results.blurb: You were lost, the map was useless, and somewhere on an unnamed road it stopped mattering. There was a shop, a view, a dog, a very good sandwich. You have been trying to get back to that accidental afternoon ever since, and the beautiful thing is you never will, and you keep going anyway.
results.watchOut: Not every wrong turn is a gift. Some are just a wrong turn. Check the fuel.

results.name: THE SONG IN THE SUPERMARKET
results.blurb: Aisle nine, mid-week, nobody around, and a song came on that you loved at fourteen. You did the small, private, extremely undignified thing: you sang. For two minutes the fluorescent lights were a stage. You have never told anyone, and it is still the memory that works best.
results.watchOut: You perform happiness for strangers more easily than you share it with friends. Invite someone to aisle nine.
